clue.text: Soft-hearted girl is something of a nut

indicators.note: a girl who is soft-hearted has the soft marking placed at her heart, so it goes inside the name

parts.note: Cora is a girl's name
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A tender-hearted young woman is described as a bit of a nutcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something of a nut' sounds like an insult to the girl, but it is the definition: part of a coconut.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried kernel of the coconut, from which oil is pressed, so it is part of a nut.

clue.text: Fall at 90º in unconscious state before army hairdresser?

indicators.note: the first group comes before the next piece
one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a coma is a state of deep unconsciousness
a compass bearing of 90 degrees is east, E
a cropper cuts hair short, as an army barber does

explanation.surface: A soldier falls into unconsciousness at a right angle before the barber's chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, so 90 degrees is east, E, which goes inside COMA.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a fall or suffer a sudden failure is idiomatically to take a heavy tumble of this kind.

clue.text: Bird changes head from what could be its doom …

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is replaced with another

parts.note: a shotgun cartridge could kill a game bird

explanation.surface: A game bird swaps its head for the thing that could kill it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 3 down. CARTRIDGE with its first letter C replaced by P gives the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump game bird shot in Britain in autumn, the target of shotgun cartridges.

clue.text: … very pale, like the female of the species

parts.note: as means like
a hen is a female bird, here the partridge of the previous clue

explanation.surface: The hen partridge is pale with fear at the thought of the gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 2 down, so 'the species' is the partridge, whose female is a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A face drained of colour from shock is the colour of ash, deathly pale.

clue.text: Prelate with determination, but having aims thwarted

parts.note: will means determination or resolve

indicators.note: plans that are thwarted are upset, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A churchman of strong resolve nonetheless sees his ambitions frustrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thwarted' scrambles IAMS from AIMS. 'But having' is just linking; 'Prelate' points to Rowan Williams, then Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowan Williams was Archbishop of Canterbury when this puzzle appeared, a senior prelate of the Church of England.

clue.text: With difficulty unmask a flasher by his appearance?

definitions.meaning: to extract or expose something with effort
a flasher appears with his willy, a slang winkle, exposed

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a cheeky British slang joke: winkle is a childish word for penis, so a flasher literally has it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise out a winkle shellfish needs a pin, so the phrase means to extract or uncover something with effort.

clue.text: Revolutionary could be back for Christmas

indicators.note: the word for Christmas is read backwards

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: A revolutionary might return for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' is Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a leading figure of the Russian Revolution, so his first name stands for a revolutionary.

clue.text: Its carbon print is evident

parts.note: a black drawing ink made from lampblack leaves a visible carbon mark on paper, playing on carbon footprint

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an environmental 'carbon footprint', but the clue describes a dense black ink made from soot.
explanation.definitionFit: This black drawing ink is made from lampblack, a form of carbon, so its marks are carbon prints.

clue.text: Worth seen in former Italian leader

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the words former Italian

explanation.surface: Value was found in an ex-leader of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'former' and the start of 'Italian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit and worth are synonyms, both meaning the quality of deserving praise.

clue.text: Right wheel … about turn … get lost …

definitions.meaning: these are parade-ground commands given to soldiers on the march
a dismissal, telling someone to leave

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the literal one, commands to marching troops; the second is the idiom for being sent packing.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill commands are literally orders for marching, and being given such orders idiomatically means being dismissed from a job or place.

clue.text: Delay mail in capital

parts.note: to block is to hold up or delay
letters are mail

explanation.surface: Post is held up in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city, but means capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Block letters are capitals written separately, as on forms.

clue.text: A false slander can get one's blood up

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing glands that pump adrenaline, standing for the noun

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so these letters are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: An untrue defamatory remark can make a person angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' rearranges A and SLANDER. The definition describes what the glands do rather than naming them, which is fair because adrenaline raises the pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands release adrenaline, the hormone that makes the heart race when one is angry or roused.

clue.text: Hilary's bookshelf?

parts.note: read as a work by the novelist Hilary ..., and also as a shelf over a fireplace on which books might stand

explanation.walkthrough: Hilary Mantel is the English novelist of Wolf Hall; a 'piece' by her is one of her books, and the whole phrase is also the shelf above a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelf above a fireplace is a familiar place to stand ornaments or books, while a piece by Hilary Mantel is one of her novels.

clue.text: Tardis, or a new heating system

indicators.note: new letters are a fresh arrangement of the old ones

explanation.surface: Doctor Who's time machine, or perhaps a fresh way of warming a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TARDIS, OR and A. The Tardis is the time machine in the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of radiators fed by a boiler is the standard central heating arrangement in a house.

clue.text: With dread as we get in a vehicle

indicators.note: the word we gets into the preceding word, so it goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: We climb into a lorry fearfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'as' as a link word, but it is the container; 'get in' signals the insertion, and the result means filled with awe.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overcome with awe means filled with wonder and dread together.

clue.text: Does it pay to salt icy roads?

definitions.text: Does it pay to salt icy roads?

parts.words: Does it pay to salt icy roads?
parts.note: read literally as money for clearing melting snow, but really money held secretly for bribes

explanation.walkthrough: Slush is the melted snow left on gritted roads; the phrase actually means a secret reserve of money used for bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret reserve of money set aside for bribery or other illicit purposes, read whimsically as cash for clearing snow.

clue.text: Investments of Israel's father

definitions.meaning: ..., an Individual Savings Account, a British tax-free investment account
Jacob, renamed Israel in Genesis, was the son of the patriarch

explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings or investment account and A/C abbreviates account, so the letters can stand for investments.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob is renamed Israel, and his father was the patriarch son of Abraham and Sarah.

clue.text: A gym shoe on board may be modified

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: dap is a West Country and Welsh word for a plimsoll or gym shoe
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A plimsoll placed on a table might be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts A DAP above TABLE. A dap is a canvas gym shoe in parts of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptable can be changed or adjusted to suit new conditions.

clue.text: See 11
Communication of old by elephant?

parts.note: an elephant trumpets through its long nose, and an old-fashioned long-distance telephone call had a name using the same word

explanation.walkthrough: Before direct dialling, a long-distance phone call in Britain went over trunk lines; an elephant's call comes through its trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The old term for a long-distance telephone call routed over main lines, punning on an elephant's nose.

clue.text: Cornish visitors encountered in German city

indicators.note: one word is placed in the other

parts.note: Ems, or Bad Ems, is a spa town in Germany
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Tourists from Cornwall were met in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmets is the Cornish dialect word for tourists (literally ants); Cornwall is a holiday county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cornish dialect the word for ants is applied to the summer tourists who swarm into the county.

clue.text: Impressionist painter swaps ends in card game

indicators.note: the two letters at the end of the name change places

parts.note: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist

explanation.surface: An Impressionist artist swaps the ends of his canvases in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the last two letters of MONET gives the gambling card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte, or three-card monte, is a gambling card game.

clue.text: Current regulator finds hearts to break

indicators.note: to break the words is to smash them into pieces and reassemble the letters

explanation.surface: Someone who controls the flow finds hearts are made to break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' scrambles HEARTS and TO; 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable resistor that controls the electrical current flowing in a circuit, as in a light dimmer.

clue.text: Christian sect drops head for dishing out the hard stuff

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a bar device, standing for the noun

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: the Coptic Church is the Egyptian Christian church

explanation.surface: Members of a Christian church stop leading worship to pour spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: COPTIC loses its first letter, signalled by 'drops head'. An optic is the measure fitted to upside-down spirit bottles in British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs this device fixed to an upturned bottle dispenses a measured shot of spirits.

clue.text: Sign of one male turning into none?

indicators.note: the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Is a single man turning into nobody a sign of something?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges ONE and M. 'Into none?' adds wit: change the M back to N and the letters give NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or sign of something to come.

clue.text: Amount blue rinse endlessly comes to is beyond solution

indicators.note: the letters come to a new arrangement, as a sum comes to a total
the word rinse has its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: The cost of a blue rinse at the hairdresser is an insoluble problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims RINSE to RINS; 'comes to' shuffles AMOUNT, BLUE and RINS together. The definition 'is beyond solution' includes 'is', describing a problem that cannot be overcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem that cannot be overcome or surmounted is beyond any solution.

clue.text: Worked out reported damage by 1 down, initially

indicators.note: the word for damage is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to wreck is to damage badly
the figure 1 read as a word

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word down is taken

explanation.surface: Calculated damage was reported from a fall, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' looks like a cross-reference to 1 down in the grid, but 1 gives ONE and 'down, initially' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reckoned a figure is to have calculated or worked it out.

clue.text: What may be pursued on board revolutionary ship

definitions.text: What may be pursued on board

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Something chased aboard a revolutionary vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship's deck, but it is a game played on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played on a board, in which pieces chase the opposing king.
